import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cherlin–Zilber conjecture

The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture (also called the algebraicity conjecture) states that an infinite
simple group whose first-order theory is stable in $\aleph_0$ (i.e. $\omega$-stable) is a simple
algebraic group over an algebraically closed field.

Mathlib has neither $\omega$-stability nor algebraic groups, so this file defines both.

* `groupLanguage` is the first-order language of groups $(\cdot, {}^{-1}, 1)$; every group is a
  structure for it.
* A theory `T` is $\omega$-stable (`IsOmegaStable`) if for every model `M` of `T` and every
  countable set `A ⊆ M` of parameters there are only countably many complete types over `A`.
* Algebraic groups over an algebraically closed field `K` are modelled classically as Zariski
  closed subgroups of `GL n K`. This loses no generality: a simple algebraic group is
  noncommutative, hence affine by Chevalley's structure theorem, hence isomorphic to a closed
  subgroup of some `GL n K`. A *simple algebraic group* is a connected noncommutative closed
  subgroup whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and itself.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- [Wikipedia, Stable group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_group)
- [Wikipedia, Simple algebraic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_algebraic_group)
- G. Cherlin, *Groups of small Morley rank*, Ann. Math. Logic 17 (1979), 1–28.
- B. I. Zil'ber, *Groups and rings whose theory is categorical*, Fundam. Math. 95 (1977),
  173–188.
-/
namespace CherlinZilberConjecture
open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
universe u v
/- ### $\omega$-stability -/

blocks.docstring:
A first-order theory `T` is *$\omega$-stable* (or *$\aleph_0$-stable*, "stable in $\aleph_0$") if
for every model `M` of `T`, every countable set `A` of parameters from `M` and every `n`, the
space $S_n^M(A)$ of complete `n`-types over `A` is countable.

Here $S_n^M(A)$ is realised as the space of complete types in `n` variables of the complete theory
of `M` in the language `L[[A]]` obtained by adding a constant symbol for each element of `A`.
As for `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`, models are taken in the universe `max u v`; by
the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Theory.CompleteType, FirstOrder.Language.completeTheory, Language.withConstants (used as building blocks); no stability notion exists in Mathlib.ModelTheory.
justification.name: CherlinZilberConjecture.IsOmegaStable
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of (ω-)stability of a theory; needed for the hypothesis 'first-order theory stable in ℵ₀'.

blocks.name: IsOmegaStable
blocks.text:
/--
A first-order theory `T` is *$\omega$-stable* (or *$\aleph_0$-stable*, "stable in $\aleph_0$") if
for every model `M` of `T`, every countable set `A` of parameters from `M` and every `n`, the
space $S_n^M(A)$ of complete `n`-types over `A` is countable.

Here $S_n^M(A)$ is realised as the space of complete types in `n` variables of the complete theory
of `M` in the language `L[[A]]` obtained by adding a constant symbol for each element of `A`.
As for `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`, models are taken in the universe `max u v`; by
the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.
-/
def IsOmegaStable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (A : Set M), A.Countable →
    ∀ n : ℕ, Countable ((L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin n))

blocks.code:
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, GroupFunc.one => 1
    | _, GroupFunc.inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, GroupFunc.mul => x 0 * x 1
  RelMap {_} r _ := (r : Empty).elim

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the symbols by the group
operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, GroupFunc.one => 1
    | _, GroupFunc.inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, GroupFunc.mul => x 0 * x 1
  RelMap {_} r _ := (r : Empty).elim

section AlgebraicGroup
variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

blocks.docstring:
A set of `n × n` matrices over `K` is *Zariski closed* if it is the common zero set of a family
of polynomials in the `n²` matrix entries.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MvPolynomial.zeroLocus (Nullstellensatz file; only for `σ → K`, so a direct polynomial zero-set definition on matrices was used), PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology (on Spec, not on K-points), Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (used), CategoryTheory Grp_ objects in Scheme (no group-scheme API).

justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no algebraic groups (no group schemes, no linear algebraic groups); a concrete notion of a (simple, connected) Zariski-closed subgroup of GL_n(K) is needed for the conclusion.

blocks.name: IsAlgebraicSubgroup
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *linear algebraic group* if it is Zariski closed in
`GL_n(K)`, i.e. it consists of the invertible matrices lying in some Zariski closed set of
matrices. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), IsZariskiClosed Z ∧
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) K, g ∈ H ↔ (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) ∈ Z

  ⟨Set.univ, isZariskiClosed_univ, by simp⟩

blocks.name: IsZariskiConnected
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is *connected* if it is connected as a subspace of `GL_n(K)` for
the Zariski topology. -/
def IsZariskiConnected (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  letI := zariskiTopology (K := K) (n := n)
  IsConnected (matrixSet H)

blocks.code:
def IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraicSubgroup H ∧ IsZariskiConnected H ∧
    (¬ ∀ a ∈ H, ∀ b ∈ H, a * b = b * a) ∧
    ∀ N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K), N ≤ H → IsAlgebraicSubgroup N → IsZariskiConnected N →
      (∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N) → N = ⊥ ∨ N = H
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *simple algebraic group* if it is a connected noncommutative
linear algebraic group whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and `H`
itself.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MvPolynomial.zeroLocus (Nullstellensatz file; only for `σ → K`, so a direct polynomial zero-set definition on matrices was used), PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology (on Spec, not on K-points), Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (used), CategoryTheory Grp_ objects in Scheme (no group-scheme API).
justification.name: CherlinZilberConjecture.IsZariskiClosed / zariskiTopology / matrixSet / IsAlgebraicSubgroup / IsZariskiConnected / IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no algebraic groups (no group schemes, no linear algebraic groups); a concrete notion of a (simple, connected) Zariski-closed subgroup of GL_n(K) is needed for the conclusion.

blocks.name: IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *simple algebraic group* if it is a connected noncommutative
linear algebraic group whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and `H`
itself. -/
def IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraicSubgroup H ∧ IsZariskiConnected H ∧
    (¬ ∀ a ∈ H, ∀ b ∈ H, a * b = b * a) ∧
    ∀ N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K), N ≤ H → IsAlgebraicSubgroup N → IsZariskiConnected N →
      (∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N) → N = ⊥ ∨ N = H
end AlgebraicGroup

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3 14 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : IsOmegaStable (groupLanguage.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture** (algebraicity conjecture). Let $G$ be an infinite simple group
whose complete first-order theory (in the language of groups) is stable in $\aleph_0$, i.e.
$\omega$-stable. Then $G$ is a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: there
are an algebraically closed field $K$ and a simple algebraic group $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ over
$K$ such that $G \cong H$ as abstract groups.

The hypothesis that $G$ is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose theories are
trivially $\omega$-stable. An infinite simple group is automatically nonabelian. Since $G$ is
abstractly simple, any Zariski closed $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with $H \cong G$ is automatically
connected, noncommutative and simple in every usual convention for simple algebraic groups.
blocks.name: cherlin_zilber_conjecture

/--
**The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture** (algebraicity conjecture). Let $G$ be an infinite simple group
whose complete first-order theory (in the language of groups) is stable in $\aleph_0$, i.e.
$\omega$-stable. Then $G$ is a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: there
are an algebraically closed field $K$ and a simple algebraic group $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ over
$K$ such that $G \cong H$ as abstract groups.

The hypothesis that $G$ is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose theories are
trivially $\omega$-stable. An infinite simple group is automatically nonabelian. Since $G$ is
abstractly simple, any Zariski closed $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with $H \cong G$ is automatically
connected, noncommutative and simple in every usual convention for simple algebraic groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 14 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : IsOmegaStable (groupLanguage.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry
end CherlinZilberConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every infinite (the article's implicit hypothesis, needed to exclude finite simple groups) nonabelian simple group G whose complete first-order theory in the language of groups is ω-stable ("stable in ℵ_0", i.e. ℵ_0-stable, strictly stronger than stable/superstable), G is isomorphic as an abstract group to the K-points of a (connected, positive-dimensional) simple algebraic group over some algebraically closed field K; the article's remark that the finite-Morley-rank special case is already hard is context, not a separately posed question.
claims.reviewer_why: c08 states: for every infinite simple group G (Mathlib IsSimpleGroup + Infinite) whose complete theory in the language {1, ⁻¹, *} is ω-stable (for every model M in Type 0, every countable A ⊆ M and every n, the space of complete n-types over A — Mathlib CompleteType of the L[[A]]-theory of M — is countable; equivalent to the textbook definition by Löwenheim–Skolem), there exist an algebraically closed field K in G's universe, n, and a Zariski-closed subgroup H ≤ GL_n(K) that is connected in the (literally constructed) Zariski topology, noncommutative, with no proper nontrivial connected closed normal subgroups, and G ≃* H as abstract groups. Modelling 'simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field' as a closed subgroup of GL_n(K) is the classical definition (linear algebraic group); simple algebraic groups are noncommutative hence affine (Chevalley) hence linear, so nothing is lost, and this is the notion used in the Cherlin–Zilber literature. Because G is abstractly simple, every convention for 'simple algebraic group' (Humphreys/Borel vs Milne, connected or not) yields the same truth value. c08 uses the literal topological notion of connectedness rather than the finite-index characterization used by c02/c05, so it depends on the fewest external theorems; K : Type u avoids the universe defect of c06. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cherlin–Zilber conjecture

The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture (also called the algebraicity conjecture) states that an infinite
simple group whose first-order theory is stable in $\aleph_0$ (i.e. $\omega$-stable) is a simple
algebraic group over an algebraically closed field.

Mathlib has neither $\omega$-stability nor algebraic groups, so this file defines both.

* `groupLanguage` is the first-order language of groups $(\cdot, {}^{-1}, 1)$; every group is a
  structure for it.
* A theory `T` is $\omega$-stable (`IsOmegaStable`) if for every model `M` of `T` and every
  countable set `A ⊆ M` of parameters there are only countably many complete types over `A`.
* Algebraic groups over an algebraically closed field `K` are modelled classically as Zariski
  closed subgroups of `GL n K`. This loses no generality: a simple algebraic group is
  noncommutative, hence affine by Chevalley's structure theorem, hence isomorphic to a closed
  subgroup of some `GL n K`. A *simple algebraic group* is a connected noncommutative closed
  subgroup whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and itself.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- [Wikipedia, Stable group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_group)
- [Wikipedia, Simple algebraic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_algebraic_group)
- G. Cherlin, *Groups of small Morley rank*, Ann. Math. Logic 17 (1979), 1–28.
- B. I. Zil'ber, *Groups and rings whose theory is categorical*, Fundam. Math. 95 (1977),
  173–188.
-/

namespace CherlinZilberConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v

/- ### $\omega$-stability -/

/--
A first-order theory `T` is *$\omega$-stable* (or *$\aleph_0$-stable*, "stable in $\aleph_0$") if
for every model `M` of `T`, every countable set `A` of parameters from `M` and every `n`, the
space $S_n^M(A)$ of complete `n`-types over `A` is countable.

Here $S_n^M(A)$ is realised as the space of complete types in `n` variables of the complete theory
of `M` in the language `L[[A]]` obtained by adding a constant symbol for each element of `A`.
As for `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`, models are taken in the universe `max u v`; by
the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.
-/
def IsOmegaStable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (A : Set M), A.Countable →
    ∀ n : ℕ, Countable ((L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin n))

/- ### The first-order language of groups -/

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: `1`, `⁻¹` and `*`. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | one : GroupFunc 0
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | mul : GroupFunc 2

/-- The first-order language of groups: the function symbols `1`, `⁻¹`, `*` and no relation
symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : FirstOrder.Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- The constant symbol `1` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev oneFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 0 := GroupFunc.one

/-- The unary function symbol `⁻¹` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev invFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 1 := GroupFunc.inv

/-- The binary function symbol `*` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev mulFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 2 := GroupFunc.mul

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the symbols by the group
operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, GroupFunc.one => 1
    | _, GroupFunc.inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, GroupFunc.mul => x 0 * x 1
  RelMap {_} r _ := (r : Empty).elim

section GroupStructure

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_oneFunc (x : Fin 0 → G) : Structure.funMap oneFunc x = 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_invFunc (a : G) : Structure.funMap invFunc ![a] = a⁻¹ := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_mulFunc (a b : G) : Structure.funMap mulFunc ![a, b] = a * b := rfl

end GroupStructure

/- ### Simple algebraic groups -/

section AlgebraicGroup

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/-- A set of `n × n` matrices over `K` is *Zariski closed* if it is the common zero set of a family
of polynomials in the `n²` matrix entries. -/
def IsZariskiClosed (S : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K),
    S = {A | ∀ p ∈ P, MvPolynomial.eval (fun ij ↦ A ij.1 ij.2) p = 0}

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_univ : IsZariskiClosed (Set.univ : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨∅, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_empty : IsZariskiClosed (∅ : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨{1}, by simp⟩

/-- The Zariski topology on `n × n` matrices over `K`: the topology whose closed sets are the
Zariski closed sets. (The Zariski closed sets are stable under finite unions and arbitrary
intersections, so generating a topology from their complements gives exactly this topology.) -/
def zariskiTopology : TopologicalSpace (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) :=
  TopologicalSpace.generateFrom {U | IsZariskiClosed Uᶜ}

/-- The set of matrices underlying a subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)`. -/
def matrixSet (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) :=
  ((↑) : GL (Fin n) K → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) '' H

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *linear algebraic group* if it is Zariski closed in
`GL_n(K)`, i.e. it consists of the invertible matrices lying in some Zariski closed set of
matrices. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), IsZariskiClosed Z ∧
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) K, g ∈ H ↔ (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) ∈ Z

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_top : IsAlgebraicSubgroup (⊤ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isZariskiClosed_univ, by simp⟩

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is *connected* if it is connected as a subspace of `GL_n(K)` for
the Zariski topology. -/
def IsZariskiConnected (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  letI := zariskiTopology (K := K) (n := n)
  IsConnected (matrixSet H)

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *simple algebraic group* if it is a connected noncommutative
linear algebraic group whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and `H`
itself. -/
def IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraicSubgroup H ∧ IsZariskiConnected H ∧
    (¬ ∀ a ∈ H, ∀ b ∈ H, a * b = b * a) ∧
    ∀ N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K), N ≤ H → IsAlgebraicSubgroup N → IsZariskiConnected N →
      (∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N) → N = ⊥ ∨ N = H

end AlgebraicGroup

/--
**The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture** (algebraicity conjecture). Let $G$ be an infinite simple group
whose complete first-order theory (in the language of groups) is stable in $\aleph_0$, i.e.
$\omega$-stable. Then $G$ is a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: there
are an algebraically closed field $K$ and a simple algebraic group $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ over
$K$ such that $G \cong H$ as abstract groups.

The hypothesis that $G$ is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose theories are
trivially $\omega$-stable. An infinite simple group is automatically nonabelian. Since $G$ is
abstractly simple, any Zariski closed $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with $H \cong G$ is automatically
connected, noncommutative and simple in every usual convention for simple algebraic groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 14 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : IsOmegaStable (groupLanguage.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end CherlinZilberConjecture

items: 'Simple group' + implicit 'infinite' (from the Stable_group article: 'infinite (ω-stable) simple groups') formalized as `[Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]`; the finite case is excluded because finite simple groups are ω-stable but are not connected algebraic groups.

'Stable in ℵ₀' read as ω-stability of the complete theory `groupLanguage.completeTheory G` (Th(G) in the language {1, ⁻¹, *}). ω-stability is defined textbook-style (Marker Def. 4.2.17 / Tent–Ziegler): for every model M, every countable parameter set A ⊆ M and every n, the space S_n^M(A) of complete n-types over A is countable; S_n^M(A) is realised as `(L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin n)`. Using all n rather than only n = 1 is a standard equivalent choice.

Following Mathlib's convention for `IsSatisfiable`/`ModelsBoundedFormula`, models in `IsOmegaStable` range over `ModelType.{u, v, max u v}` (here `Type 0`); by Löwenheim–Skolem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.

'Simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field' formalized concretely as a Zariski-closed subgroup H of GL_n(K) (K algebraically closed, any n) that is connected in the Zariski topology, noncommutative, and whose closed connected normal subgroups are only ⊥ and H (Humphreys/Borel definition; the variant that also forbids finite normal subgroups is equivalent here because G ≅ H is abstractly simple). Every affine algebraic group is a closed subgroup of some GL_n, and a simple algebraic group is affine, so nothing is lost. Under the hypotheses on G these algebraic-side conditions are in fact automatic for any closed H ≅ G, so the statement is robust to the choice of variant.

The Zariski topology on n×n matrices is defined as `TopologicalSpace.generateFrom` of the complements of Zariski-closed sets (common zero sets of sets of polynomials in the n² entries); since Zariski-closed sets are closed under finite unions and arbitrary intersections this is exactly the Zariski topology. Closed subgroups of GL_n(K) are those of the form {g ∈ GL_n(K) | g ∈ Z} with Z Zariski-closed in M_n(K).
The isomorphism is of abstract groups: `Nonempty (G ≃* H)`. The field K is quantified in the same universe as G (`Type u`); this is harmless since |K| ≤ |G| for any such H(K) ≅ G.
Normality of N in H is written explicitly as ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N.

reviewer_notes:
Statement ambiguities: (1) 'simple group' must be read as *infinite* simple group (finite simple groups have ω-stable theories); the Stable group article says 'infinite (ω-stable) simple groups', and all candidates add [Infinite G]. Nonabelian is automatic for infinite simple groups, so it is not added separately (c01/c03/c04 add it redundantly — harmless). (2) 'stable in ℵ₀' = ω-stable (ℵ₀-stable), read the same way by every candidate. (3) 'simple algebraic group' convention is immaterial under the hypotheses since G is abstractly simple.

Candidate verdicts: c01, c02, c03, c04, c05, c08 are all faithful up to provably-equivalent conventions (types over countable sets vs countable models; 1-types vs n-types; finite-index vs topological connectedness; irreducible vs connected; Humphreys vs Milne simplicity; affine-algebraic-set-with-polynomial-law vs closed subgroup of GL_n). c04 has extra Mathlib imports and AMS '03' (style); c01/c03 use let-bound instances (style). c06 is REJECTED: it quantifies ∃ K : Type* in a universe independent of G : Type*; with K's universe 0 and G = PSL₂(K₀) for a huge algebraically closed K₀ in Type 1, no K in Type 0 can have |H(K)| = |G|, so the universe-polymorphic statement is false — an over-strong formalization. c07's bail-out ('matrix groups are an unfaithful surrogate') is not convincing: Zariski-closed subgroups of GL_n(K) are exactly the classical linear algebraic groups over K, simple algebraic groups are affine hence linear, and this is the framework of Borovik–Nesin / Altınel–Borovik–Cherlin. Positive-dimensionality is implied by connected + noncommutative (a connected finite algebraic group is trivial), so it need not be stated separately. Final file is c08 with docstring edits and AMS 3 14 20; compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
